svg.title: AD DNS Deprecation Impact
svg.desc: Two-column comparison: what AD DNS provides today (six record classes maintained automatically by Active Directory) versus what happens at deprecation without explicit governance
svg.text: AD DNS TODAY — what it provides
Six record classes maintained automatically by Active Directory
WHAT HAPPENS AT DEPRECATION —
without explicit governance
Kerberos SRV records
_kerberos._tcp and _kerberos._udp enable KDC
discovery for every Kerberos authentication request
RFC 2782 · registered by Netlogon at domain join
Kerberos SRV gone
Authentication fails for every Kerberos-dependent
application and service — silently, at next ticket renewal
No fallback; NTLM may mask the failure temporarily
LDAP SRV records
_ldap._tcp enables DC discovery for group membership,
policy application, and user attribute lookup
Also: _ldap._tcp.pdc._msdcs for PDC targeting
LDAP SRV gone
LDAP queries fail; GPO cannot apply; AD-integrated
applications lose directory access and attribute resolution
Affects Java apps, Linux hosts, and network devices
DC Locator records
Dynamic A and SRV records registered by Netlogon
at boot, enabling site-aware DC and GC selection
_msdcs subtree; updated on every DC restart
DC Locator gone
Machines cannot find DCs even if DCs still exist;
domain join, logon, and policy enforcement all fail
Cached credentials may hide the failure until reboot
DFS Namespace records
A and CNAME records enabling UNC file access
for roaming profiles, home drives, and shared storage
\\domain\share paths resolve through DFS A records
DFS Namespace records gone
File share access breaks silently; roaming profiles
and home drives become unreachable at next logon
No error message — UNC path simply does not resolve
Global Catalog SRV records
_gc._tcp.<forest> enables cross-domain and forest-wide
directory queries in multi-domain environments
Required for UPN logon and Exchange address lookup
Global Catalog gone
Cross-domain queries fail; forest-wide group
membership resolution breaks; UPN logon fails
Exchange Online hybrid connectors lose directory contact
Conditional Forwarding
AD DNS holds forwarding rules for on-premises
namespaces, cloud zones, and partner namespaces
The only resolver that knows about private cloud zones
Forwarding rules lost
On-premises and namespace forwarding disappears;
split-brain DNS returns across all surfaces instantly
Private cloud endpoints become unresolvable on-premises
These records do not migrate automatically.
Every one must be explicitly reprovisioned in the new DNS system
before the last domain controller is decommissioned.
